problem: VLM-based object navigation either queries the VLM densely (too slow, or forced onto weak small VLMs) or abstracts the environment into text, semantic maps or scene graphs. The abstraction separates high-level decisions from the raw visual evidence and makes them depend on upstream modules.
motivation: The bottleneck is the decision interface between the VLM and the robot, not only the VLM's capability. A good interface should call the VLM only at decision-critical moments, expose raw images, and constrain outputs to geometrically executable goals. Sparse, map-grounded choices would also make decisions verifiable, so RL with verifiable rewards can train local VLMs without CoT labels.
key_idea: Formulate object navigation as sparse selection among Points of Interest (PoIs), each coupling an executable waypoint with raw egocentric observations (frontiers, suspect objects, stairs, floor summaries), with the VLM choosing the next PoI and a low-level planner executing motion.
insight: Keeping raw images as the VLM input scales better with model capacity than text abstractions (scaling figure, PIGEON and WMNav vs. abstraction-based methods). Ablations show Object PoI is the most critical component: HM3D v1 SR falls from 67.1 to 56.2 without it. Stair Summary matters most for multi-floor: HM3D Mul SR drops from 35.9 to 25.2. RLVR with distance-scaled soft rewards on PoI choices improves SR and SPL. Entropy and output length rise rather than collapse, so it is not mere confidence sharpening.
method: PoI generation: Frontier PoIs come from newly explored boundaries of a BEV occupancy map (VLFM-style). Suspect Object PoIs are viewpoints around detected candidates (YOLOv7/OWLv2 + MobileSAM, 3D fusion as in ApexNav), with the target confirmed when confidence exceeds τ_target=0.70. Stair PoIs come from staircase detection plus a height map of sinking regions.
Memory Complement: stores each step's image with position, angle and BEV frustum, then uses a greedy maximum-coverage selection to attach extra observations to PoIs.

VLM-based PoI selection: numbered circular markers for PoIs are projected onto raw images (Mem2Ego-style). The VLM outputs a marker id, or 0 if unsure. The n_prox=4 nearest PoIs are shown, and a low-level PointNav RNN executes motion between PoIs.
Anti-stagnation: after 40 steps without reaching a PoI, the VLM sees reference images and a colored trajectory BEV and can ban the PoI area (r=3 m).

Multi-floor policy: Exploration Degree (S/L) and Stuck Degree (t/S) trigger a Floor Summary PoI of 6 MCP-selected images. If the VLM decides to leave the floor, the agent picks a Stair PoI and climbs using a StairNav RNN trained with VER on HM3D train.
Object confirmation: the VLM validates suspect objects from multi-view images (True/False/Unconfirmed/Outdoor), and detector confidence is rescaled accordingly.

RLVR pipeline: GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-7B with think/answer format. Frontier reward is distance-scaled, (d_max−d_j)/(d_max−d_min), with the mean reward as fallback for output 0. Confirmation reward is binary on pixel count. Data is collected with a distance-aware ε-greedy policy, and training uses online filtering and no KL loss.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) for PIGEON-ZeroShot; Qwen2.5-VL-7B (GRPO fine-tuned) for PIGEON-RLVR; plus YOLOv7, OWLv2, MobileSAM, PointNav RNN and StairNav RNN
setting.training_data: ZeroShot: none for the VLM, but the StairNav RNN is trained on the HM3Dv1 train split. RLVR: 38.7k training and 1.62k validation questions built from simulator trajectories with automatic rewards (305 steps, 8×H100, ~50h).
setting.action_space: PoI waypoints chosen by the VLM; low-level PointNav/StairNav RNN executes discrete actions
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, MP3D) plus real robots
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle-free); shortest-path distances are used only for RLVR rewards

numbers.extra: StairNav RNN trained on HM3Dv1 train

numbers_note: Split is reported as 'val' for Habitat validation sets. Scaling results appear only in a figure. Real-world results (20 episodes, wheeled robot): PIGEON-7B SR 95%, 48.91s, 6.2 VLM calls.
results: PIGEON-ZeroShot reaches SR/SPL of 67.1/35.8 on HM3Dv1, 79.6/38.1 on HM3Dv2 and 52.6/18.5 on MP3D, beating the best oracle-free baselines (ASCENT 65.4 SR on HM3Dv1, ApexNav 76.2 on HM3Dv2, WMNav 45.4 on MP3D). STRIVE, which uses an oracle planner, is competitive or better on MP3D. RLVR lifts Qwen2.5-VL-7B on HM3Dv2 from 72.66/33.16 to 77.56/36.55, and on A-EQA it matches SR (52.5) with higher SPL (47.4).
limitations: Depends on open-vocabulary detectors, which are ambiguous for structural categories like stairs and add VLM overhead.
Single-target only, with no persistent raw-observation memory for multi-target or sequential tasks.

SPL gains are modest because VLM calls are sparse, and the zero-shot variant still uses a trained StairNav/PointNav policy. The zero-shot model is GPT-4o, and the small RLVR model is evaluated mostly on HM3Dv2 and in the real world.
